results.title: Slow Internet Speeds Troubleshooting
results.snippet: 1. **Weak modem signal** — downstream signal below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV indicates line issues. 2. **WiFi interference or distance** — 2.4 GHz band congestion; customer too far from router. 3. **Peak-hour congestion** — shared neighbourhood node oversubscribed in the evenings (6–10 PM).

results.title: WiFi vs. Ethernet — Troubleshooting Connectivity Differences
results.snippet: | Factor | Ethernet (wired) | WiFi (wireless) | |---|---|---| | Speed | Full subscribed tier | Up to 80% of tier (varies by band) |

results.title: Device Compatibility — Approved Modems and Routers
results.snippet: Customers must use a modem on the ISP-approved list to receive full technical support. Unapproved modems may work but are not guaranteed to provision correctly or receive remote management commands (including `reboot_modem_remotely`).

<analysis>
I've gathered the following diagnostic evidence:

**Customer Context:** Jane Smith, active account since 2021, Gigabit 500 service tier in northeast (ZIP 10001), using NETGEAR CM500 modem [tool:lookup_customer].

**Modem Status:** The modem is technically online but severely degraded [tool:check_modem_status]:
- Downstream signal: -12 dBmV (well outside acceptable range; normal is -7 to +7 dBmV)
- Upstream signal: 44 dBmV (also outside normal range)
- Signal quality: weak
- 7 restarts in the last 24 hours (indicates instability)
- Uptime only 0.5 hours (just rebooted)

**Network Connectivity:** Ping test shows high latency (287 ms) and 12.5% packet loss, confirming the signal issue [tool:ping_customer_modem].

**Outage Status:** No active ISP outages in the customer's area [tool:check_isp_outage].

**Root Cause:** The orange lights and connectivity loss are caused by **weak/out-of-range signal levels** on the line, not a service outage. The KB article on slow speeds [kb:slow_speeds] confirms that downstream signal below -7 dBmV indicates a line issue. The frequent restarts suggest the modem is struggling to maintain connection due to poor signal quality.

**Next Steps:** This is a line-quality issue that likely requires an ISP technician visit to check the cable line, splitters, and connections. A remote reboot won't resolve an underlying signal problem.
</analysis>

<reply>
I'm seeing that your modem is having trouble connecting because the signal coming into it is too weak — that's what's causing those orange lights. This isn't something a simple restart will fix; it looks like there may be an issue with the cable line itself or the connections leading to your modem. I'd like to get a technician out to check your line and make sure everything is connected properly. Can I schedule that for you?
</reply>
